title: StreamGrid: Streaming Point Cloud Analytics via Compulsory Splitting and Deterministic Termination
problem: Point cloud processing accelerators generate frequent off-chip memory traffic because conventional line-buffer streaming techniques—which eliminate off-chip traffic for image-based workloads—cannot be applied to point clouds due to their irregular, non-grid computation patterns that cause unpredictable data access boundaries and non-deterministic termination conditions.
motivation: Point clouds are increasingly critical for autonomous driving, robotics, and AR/VR, but the energy cost of off-chip DRAM traffic in current accelerators limits their deployability on edge devices.
method: StreamGrid solves a memory bottleneck in point cloud processors: point clouds have irregular, unpredictable data access patterns that break conventional streaming buffers—systems that efficiently prefetch data by assuming regular access patterns like those in images. The solution uses two techniques: compulsory splitting, which divides the point cloud into fixed-size grid cells to make data access predictable and keep it all in on-chip memory; and deterministic termination, which precomputes when each processor finishes so the system avoids stalling while waiting for memory. Together, these enable point cloud processors to use the same efficient streaming approach that already works for images. An automated optimizer then minimizes the on-chip memory (SRAM) needed to maintain accuracy.
key_novelty: By partitioning point clouds into fixed-size regions and precomputing when processing finishes, StreamGrid enables point cloud processors to use conventional streaming buffers—systems designed for regular, predictable data access.
contributions: Compulsory splitting technique that bounds on-chip working sets for irregular point cloud computations.
Deterministic termination analysis that eliminates unpredictable stalls in streaming point cloud accelerators.
StreamGrid framework with automated on-chip SRAM buffer sizing.
10x speedup and 3.9x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art accelerators; 61.3% on-chip memory reduction and 40.5% energy reduction vs. baselines without these techniques.

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 3.9x energy efficiency over state-of-the-art accelerators; 40.5% energy reduction vs. baselines

baselines: state-of-the-art point cloud accelerators without streaming techniques
limitations: Marginal accuracy loss due to compulsory spatial splitting may impact point cloud segmentation tasks requiring fine boundary precision.
primary_theme: streaming point cloud analytics via spatial splitting and deterministic termination
